status: MODELED: effective-medium mixing, transmit model, thin-cylinder eddy decay; constituent values ASSUMED except the 3M iM30K data

im30k.src: 3M product information (iM30K density, calculated k; series dielectric constant)

phase_change.note: a phase-change additive only delays the rise; the steady heat still has to leave through the module wall

claims.claim: iM30K glass bubbles: real 3M product, 0.6 g/cc, high crush strength
claims.evidence: 3M table: 0.60 g/cc (0.57-0.63), 28,000 psi 90 % survival (data sheet Rev C: 27,000)

claims.claim: BN / alumina at 10-15 vol% gives > 3 W/mK
claims.evidence: Bruggeman with 45 % bubbles: 0.313-0.346 W/mK (BN), 0.312-0.344 (alumina); 3 W/mK needs about 34 vol% BN or 37 vol% alumina with no bubbles

claims.claim: the mix is invisible to the TX / RX coils (mu_r = 1)
claims.evidence: magnetically yes; electrically no: er 2.31-3.08 raises the coil capacitance; injected through the windings the quiet time misses the first gate in every case (see coil)
no product data sheet; a rigid epoxy also loads the precision parts (AB1 offsets) and solder joints by CTE mismatch: the soft gel was chosen there for that reason

claims.claim: microballoons damp vibration and remove bump false targets
claims.evidence: rigid potting stops winding / lead motion (the real microphonic source); glass bubbles in a rigid epoxy add little damping; bump signals from coil-to-ground motion are not removed by any potting

claims.claim: BN removes hot spots on the driver chips in the head
claims.evidence: the head has no driver: the FETs and clamp are in the neck module (boost about 3.9 W there); the head dissipates 0.67-1.38 W and peaks at 50.6 C at 40 C ambient (limit 80 C)

claims.claim: a single compound filling the whole head with conductive filler would ruin detection
claims.evidence: eddy rule (CLAUDE.md 5): no conductive filler anywhere

claims.claim: paint the circuit cavity with grounded conductive shield paint
claims.evidence: a closed painted wall around the axis is a closed loop (eddy rule 5): see paint; graphite paint decays too fast to matter but shields little; a slit / comb pattern with one ground point keeps the electric shielding and breaks the loop

zones.why: every fill misses the first gate: proposed matrix margin -0.201 to -1.501 us
a rigid epoxy loads the AB1 precision op-amps / ADC and the FFC joints by cure shrinkage and CTE mismatch (offset drift); the gel locks without stress

zones.use: epoxy + glass bubbles (no thermal powder needed)
zones.why: only the RX leads are there: a rigid lock stops lead motion (microphonics); their capacitance change is to be measured (PT3)
magnetic absorber function; not a structural fill

zones.use: TC silicone, or epoxy with about 34 vol% BN and no bubbles (3 W/mK class)
zones.why: the clamp bank and FETs dissipate about 3.9 W at boost; the proposed 12.5 % BN mix models at 0.313-0.346 W/mK, too low for the hot zone

zones.use: the proposed mix (epoxy + 45 % iM30K + silica; BN optional)
zones.why: structural, waterproof, 1.09 g/cc vs 0.6-0.8 for syntactic silicone: about +25 g
locks PM2 and the power leads; about +11 g over syntactic silicone
the Hall switch reads the magnet through the wall: non-magnetic fill, no change
antenna, LED light, RX-coil capacitance, serviceable pads (potting map)

zones.epoxy_matrix: NPM hot zone only, after PT5
zones.use: 11.8-15.7 g microencapsulated PCM buffers 10 min of boost
zones.why: the head runs cool (peak 50.6 C at 40 C ambient): no head zone needs it; no NPM thermal model exists, so the bench decides

zones.use: comb / slit pattern, one ground point, on the CB1D cavity only if a bench test shows pickup; inside the head only a non-magnetic paint (no nickel: MG 841AR is ferromagnetic, see product_fit)
zones.why: a closed painted wall around the axis is a closed eddy loop (rule 5); the copper-cloth septum already screens the analog cell

TC832.name: MG Chemicals 832TC thermally conductive epoxy (TDS Ver. 4.3, 04 Feb 2026)
TC832.cure: 96 h at 25 C, or 2 h 65 C / 1 h 80 C / 45 min 100 C

NI841.name: MG Chemicals 841AR Super Shield nickel conductive coating (TDS Rev. 7.0, 17 Sept 2026; older TDS Ver. 2.05, 31 Oct 2017)
NI841.solvent: acetone, dimethyl carbonate, heptan-2-one (etches ABS / PC; Ver 2.05)
NI841.adhesion_5B: ABS, PC, polyamide, PVC, FR4 (Rev 7.0); PETG not listed
NI841.cure: 24 h at 25 C or 30 min at 65 C

IM30K.name: 3M Glass Bubbles iM30K data sheet (owner copy)

product_fit.zone: NPM main, U3, U1, L1 gallery (option)
product_fit.why: data sheet: 0.6 g/cc, crush 27000 psi at 90 % survival, 18 um: survives hand mixing and vacuum de-airing; lowers density and er of any resin it goes into
er 3.7 (DF 0.1) at 1 MHz: quiet-time margin -0.501 to -2.091 us neat, -0.211 to -1.231 us with 45 % iM30K; all below the first gate

the only fill with a printed conductivity: 0.7 W/mK, about twice the proposed bubble mix; dielectric strength 15.2 kV/mm against the 460 V flyback nodes (1 mm of fill holds about 33x); Tg only 50 C: above it the epoxy softens and its CTE stays 114 ppm/C (service to 175 C), so PT5 must log the hot-zone temperature; 27000 cP: pour and vacuum de-air (vacuum 25 inHg about 2 min), no needle injection

product_fit.zone: NPM main, U3 PM2 bay, U1 HB2 pocket
product_fit.fit: YES (after a trial mix, PT1 / PT7)
product_fit.why: modeled er 2.36-2.85, k 0.427 W/mK, 1.205 g/cc (neat 832TC 1.7 g/cc: about 31 g more in the NPM main zone); 832TC is already filled, so 45 % bubbles on top may not pour: the trial mix decides the bubble fraction (start at 20-30 %)
Shore 81 D, 1.4 % shrinkage, CTE 142 ppm/C: loads the precision parts and joints; the soft gel stays
er 3.7 next to the RX leads adds lead capacitance; the bubble mix (er 2.36-2.85) is the better lock there

product_fit.zone: head: vault, CB1D cavity, anywhere inside the coil field
product_fit.why: eddy decay is not the problem (tau 0.0173-0.0953 us at 0.29-1.6 ohm/sq, gone long before the 5.91 us gate); the problem is the nickel: ferromagnetic, relative permeability >= 100 (Ver 2.05), a magnetic surface the TX field magnetises on every pulse; its remanence and magnetic viscosity are not on either sheet (UNVERIFIED), so it may leave a slow tail in the RX window; the eddy rule (5) forbids a closed painted wall anyway

product_fit.zone: neck module (NPM) inner wall, outside the coil field
product_fit.why: screens the 460 V switching node; comb / slit pattern with one ground point (rule 5); PETG adhesion not on the sheet and the acetone solvent etches some plastics: coupon test PT7; PT9 checks the RX tail with a painted coupon at the coil
